The main takeaway from our work is that
Milton is engaged in an Epicurean polemic throughout the whole of Paradise Lost, not only in the invocations, but also in the main narrative.
Milton’s poem is not a straightforward narrative of the Fall, but rather a complex meditation on the nature of the Fall and its implications for the human condition.
Milton’s poem about the Fall is a poem about the poet’s own fear of falling, a fear that is both a source and a product of his engagement with Lucretius.
